pairs.why: A's palm has the chunky, frame-filling leaves and thick segmented trunk of the real card, while B is smaller and thinner.
B's tall barrel with smooth wood staves and metal hoops is built like a real barrel, as in the reference cards, while A is a squat toy pot with a knobbed lid on an off-palette grey floor.
B is a full-volume saucer with soft glossy highlights and a sensible underside, like the real cards' clay-smooth icons, while A reads as a flat disc seen from above.
B's smoother, cleaner plastic is nearer the real bottle's soft finish, while A's ribbed grip details push it toward the texture-y look the lessons reject, though B is a little too saturated.
A hangs on the wall with a thick glossy bevelled rim and a soft wall shadow like the real clock, while B stands on a floor with a flatter rim.
A's chunky, smooth stone table with a framed board matches the real card's stylized mass, while B is slimmer and has more marble-vein texture.
B keeps the dark navy body nearly free of accents, like the real light, while A adds an orange band that isn't on the real card; otherwise the two are close.
B's green support posts, softer green slide and yellow platform match the real slide's colors and build, while A switches to lime and blue pillars and adds a toy-like splash.
